speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to your post-operative evaluation. You mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy
REQUEST IMAGES: Ear_Microscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The otoscopy and microscopy show normal readings, so the difficulty with earrings might not be due to active infection or gross structural failure. Did you notice any fluid drainage from the ear, or does the pain seem to radiate to your jaw when you chew? REQUEST TEST: Pure_Tone_Audiometry

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms the ear canal and tympanic membrane appear intact, which is good news. However, since the pain is specifically triggered by wearing earrings, I need to know if you can still hear clearly at your baseline or if you are experiencing any ringing in the ear. REQUEST TEST: Pure_Tone_Audiometry. Also, do you have a history of diabetes or a compromised immune system, as this affects healing?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The audiometry confirms normal hearing, and since the otoscopy was clear, this points away from a simple infection or structural graft failure. Do you experience pain only when the earring touches the ear canal, or does it hurt to chew and move your jaw? Also, have you noticed any new lumps or swelling in front of your ear?

REQUEST TEST: Temporal_Bone_CT_Scan
REQUEST IMAGES: Ear_Microscopy

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CT scan and microscopy are normal, ruling out deep infection or graft displacement; does the pain worsen specifically when you move your jaw or chew, and do you have any numbness or tingling in your lower lip or chin? Also, has the pain persisted since the surgery or did it start later?

REQUEST TEST: Neurological_Examination_of_Facial_Nerve
REQUEST IMAGES: Ear_Microscopy

speaker: Doctor
text:
The neurological exam is normal, so facial nerve injury is unlikely. Given your normal imaging and hearing, is there any specific sensation like numbness or tingling in your earlobe, or does the pain feel like a sharp electric shock when the earring touches the skin? Also, have you noticed any small blisters or redness on the pinna?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-herpetic neuralgia or localized neuropathic pain post-tympanoplasty.
